svg.title: RAG & Document Retrieval
svg.desc: Proposed RAG design drill-down for the Enterprise AI Agent Sales and Risk System, not live integrations. Knowledge Ingestion consumes the existing governed ETL outputs from the internal database and authorized Gmail mailboxes. Source labels represent upstream sources, not separate direct-to-model database or mailbox connections. Restricted S3 originals remain accessible only to ingestion roles. They are not accessible to the agent retrieval role. Read-only database changes and Gmail content carry source identity, version, deletion state and access metadata. Permissions and Sensitive Fields uses authoritative customer/project mappings and document ACLs. Unknown ownership or missing scope is quarantined, never guessed into an accessible project by a model. Sensitive data is classified, removed, masked or retained by approved business purpose before the retrieval corpus is published. Every derived chunk inherits its document's ACL; attachments and mixed-project documents require independently validated scope. Airflow task workers parse content and split by sections, tables and meaningful email replies, reducing repeated quoted history. Chunking never joins documents with different permissions. Parser and chunker versions are recorded. Text chunks are evidence, not executable instructions. Numerical source-of-truth records remain governed SQL facts. Versioned Chunks in Snowflake contain customer/project scope, document and chunk identity, source version, source timestamp, content hash, source/page/message references, classification, ACL and deletion status. Incremental jobs process changed documents and tombstones idempotently. Cortex Search indexes only the approved retrieval corpus. Its hosted embedding, keyword and reranking processing must use enterprise-approved models, regions and service settings. Search refresh has independent freshness status; the Published Index connector means published searchable versions, not instantaneous global consistency. Revocations are immediately enforced at serving reauthorization; index and cache cleanup follow, so stale indexed permissions cannot grant access. Scoped Retrieval begins with an authenticated manager request through the existing application. Backend code resolves the user's current customer, project and document entitlements. AWS IAM governs AWS service access; application policy and Snowflake roles implement business authorization. IAM alone is not customer-level document authorization. The model cannot choose the user's identity, widen the scope, remove ACL filters or select an unrestricted index. Hybrid Search and Reranking uses Cortex Search through a trusted backend retrieval service. Mandatory customer, project and document filters are inserted by backend code; least-privileged service credentials never reach clients or models. Cortex Search uses owner's rights, so underlying table row policies are not assumed to automatically restrict caller results. Service/index boundaries are separated where policy requires; filters are not client options. Read-Only SQL is a separate branch for authoritative order, cost, capacity and risk facts in governed Snowflake views. It uses approved parameterized queries, enforced scope, restricted roles, timeouts, concurrency and result limits. Agent-authored arbitrary SQL and unrestricted raw database credentials are not exposed by this tool interface. Authorized Evidence Pack is assembled by a FastAPI backend. It rechecks each result against current entitlements, source version and deletion status before entering the model context, drops unauthorized material, flags stale or conflicting evidence, deduplicates and selects minimum necessary context under a token budget. Critical gaps block quote generation or require clarification. It records citations and an as-of/source-version manifest; this does not claim a distributed transaction across sources. SQL results carry units, currencies and authoritative source IDs. Multi-Agent Analysis runs the existing LangGraph business and engineering workflow on AWS Bedrock AgentCore. Agents receive role-relevant excerpts and structured facts from the same scoped evidence manifest, not full archives. Only enterprise-approved models may process this context; provider, region, retention and logging policies apply to generation, embeddings, reranking and evaluation. Private connectivity is not the same as enterprise self-hosting. Project memory is retrievable source history and approved project state, not model weight training or shared customer memory. Session state and cache keys include authorized user/customer/project scope and source/policy versions; permissions are revalidated on every request. Logs avoid unnecessary full document and cost contents. Retrieval quality, citation coverage, access isolation and stale-version failures feed the existing Agent Eval module; telemetry arrows are omitted from this overview for clarity. No new standalone vector database is introduced. Two lanes, orthogonal non-crossing arrows and 32px logos match the other drill-downs. No other diagram is changed.
